stages.name: Requirements
stages.entryQuestion: Before designing a chat service, what scope and scale assumptions would you clarify?
stages.objective: Agree on product behavior, measurable quality targets and the stated exercise workload.

completionCriteria.name: Functional scope
completionCriteria.guidance: Clarify online/offline delivery, group bounds, media references and acknowledgement meanings; typing indicators are optional.

completionCriteria.name: Quality targets
completionCriteria.guidance: Separate accepted, delivered and read states; order within a conversation rather than globally.

completionCriteria.name: Capacity estimates
completionCriteria.guidance: Use the fictional baseline or state a justified alternative; derive average and peak rates and distinguish payload bytes from replication and indexes.

stages.name: High Level Design
stages.entryQuestion: Walk me through online and offline message delivery at a high level.
stages.objective: Separate connection routing, durable messaging and asynchronous notifications.

completionCriteria.name: Connection routing
completionCriteria.guidance: Route authenticated persistent connections to a connection server; WebSocket or an equivalent transport is acceptable.

completionCriteria.name: Durable messaging
completionCriteria.guidance: Assign message persistence and recipient delivery to a messaging service and durable store.

completionCriteria.name: Offline and media paths
completionCriteria.guidance: Describe offline backlog access and media stored outside the message database.

stages.name: Core Flow
stages.entryQuestion: How do retries, acknowledgements and ordering work when a phone disconnects?
stages.objective: Provide practical at-least-once delivery with deduplication and bounded ordering.

completionCriteria.name: Acknowledgement boundary
completionCriteria.guidance: Distinguish server acceptance from recipient delivery and read receipts; persist before acceptance ACK.

completionCriteria.name: Retry deduplication
completionCriteria.guidance: Use a stable client message ID so reconnect retries do not create duplicate visible messages.

completionCriteria.name: Conversation ordering
completionCriteria.guidance: Choose per-conversation sequence allocation or a justified alternative; handle gaps and duplicate arrivals.

completionCriteria.name: Group fanout
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain bounded group membership lookup and per-recipient delivery without promising a global order across chats.

stages.name: Data Model
stages.entryQuestion: What keys and indexes let a device fetch unread messages in order?
stages.objective: Model conversations, membership and messages with cursor-based reads.

completionCriteria.name: Message schema
completionCriteria.guidance: Key messages by conversation and sequence or equivalent sortable cursor; store sender, stable message ID and payload reference.

completionCriteria.name: Membership and cursors
completionCriteria.guidance: Represent group membership and per-device delivered/read cursors while enforcing access.

completionCriteria.name: Retention and pagination
completionCriteria.guidance: Use cursor pagination and an explicit retention policy; do not retain media inline in text rows.

stages.name: Reliability
stages.entryQuestion: What happens if connection servers, the broker or the message store fail?
stages.objective: Recover delivery from durable state rather than transient Pub/Sub.

completionCriteria.name: Durable replay
completionCriteria.guidance: A transient Redis Pub/Sub channel alone is not an offline message store; replay from durable messages or a durable log.

completionCriteria.name: Reconnect recovery
completionCriteria.guidance: Handle reconnect storms, exponential backoff and stale connection ownership.

completionCriteria.name: Safe notifications
completionCriteria.guidance: Push notifications are hints, not proof of delivery; respect membership changes and avoid leaking private media.

stages.name: Scaling
stages.entryQuestion: How would you size and partition this chat workload without creating a hot group shard?
stages.objective: Scale connections, writes and fanout independently.

completionCriteria.name: Partitioning
completionCriteria.guidance: Choose conversation-based ownership for message order; distribute unrelated conversations independently.

completionCriteria.name: Traffic and storage
completionCriteria.guidance: Derive 4629.63 sent messages/s average, 23148.15 peak and 3.6 TB raw text retention for 30 days.

completionCriteria.name: Backpressure
completionCriteria.guidance: Bound queues and isolate busy groups or users; avoid a single global broker partition.

stages.name: Tradeoffs
stages.entryQuestion: What guarantees would you trade for availability, latency and battery use?
stages.objective: Explain transport, delivery and storage tradeoffs without requiring a specific broker.

completionCriteria.name: Delivery tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Compare at-least-once plus dedupe with the cost and limits of end-to-end exactly-once claims.

completionCriteria.name: Consistency tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain ordering and membership correctness during partitions, not only a memorized CAP slogan.

completionCriteria.name: Transport tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Compare persistent connections with polling or streaming alternatives and their mobile-resource costs.
